title: A SURVEY ON FAIRNESS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN E-COMMERCE: PROGRESS, APPLICATION, AND CHALLENGE

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated intrinsically using similarity-based metrics (WEAT, SEAT, CEAT) to calculate cosine similarity between gendered attribute words and target words, and extrinsically using benchmarks like BOLD and Counterfactual Sentiment Bias (CSB) to assess sentiment, toxicity, and regard differences across counterfactual prompts.

Measured intrinsically via word embedding associations and extrinsically using benchmark datasets like BOLD and CSB to evaluate disparities in sentiment, toxicity, and emotion in language generation based on racial identities.

Evaluated using extrinsic evaluation metrics and comprehensive benchmark datasets like BOLD to measure sentiment, toxicity, and regard in open-ended text generated from prompts describing religious target populations.
Assessed using the BOLD benchmark dataset to evaluate completions generated by language models for differences in sentiment, toxicity, and emotion lexicons based on political ideology.

Evaluated by analyzing the skewed distribution of visibility and user attention among items or sellers in recommendation systems, and measured through multi-process fusion methods or exposure adjustments.

Assessed by analyzing how search results are skewed towards certain products or sellers, and evaluated by measuring mitigation performance (e.g., F1 score improvements) using iterative learning frameworks like TripleLearn.
Evaluated by comparing the noise and inaccuracy of seller-provided textual metadata against the performance of automated, search-boosted tag recommenders derived from consumer query and click data.
